subject: gk
question:
Fill in the blank:

The Indian Councils Act 1892 for the first time permitted legislative councils to _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**discuss the annual budget**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Councils Act of 1892** marked a significant milestone in India's legislative history as it allowed for the legislative councils to **discuss the annual budget** for the first time. This was a step towards increasing the role of Indians in legislative processes.
 
• The Act introduced the provision of asking **questions on public matters**, giving members of legislative councils a platform to raise concerns and hold the administration accountable.
 
• Though the Act allowed discussions on the budget, **it did not permit voting on it**, limiting the influence of the councils over financial matters.
 
• The Act also expanded the size of the legislative councils, both at the **central and provincial levels**, thus involving more members in governance.
 
• It introduced the concept of **indirect elections** to the councils, though the majority of the members were still nominated by the British government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Councils Act, 1892:**

 
 
• This Act was an amendment to the **Indian Councils Act of 1861**.
 
• It allowed for the **non-official members** of the councils to discuss budgetary matters, marking a step towards more inclusive governance.
 
• The councils were expanded in size, and **representation of Indians** was increased, paving the way for further reforms.
 
 
 
• **Key limitations of the Act:**
 
 
• The role of Indians in governance was still largely advisory, with no substantial powers granted to them.
 
• The discussions on the budget were limited to certain parts, and **voting rights were absent**.
 
• The members of the councils were primarily nominated, with only a few being indirectly elected.
 
 
 
• **Subsequent Reforms:**
 
 
• The **Indian Councils Act of 1909** (also known as the Morley-Minto reforms) introduced further changes, such as the inclusion of **separate electorates for Muslims**.
 
• Later, the **Government of India Act of 1919** introduced the concept of diarchy in provinces, granting more administrative powers to Indians.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Act:**
 
 
• The Act of 1892 was an important step in the process of India's **political awakening**.
 
• It laid the foundation for future demands for **self-governance** and greater representation of Indians in legislative bodies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Legislative Councils:**

 
 
• The legislative councils under the Act were mainly advisory in nature, with their recommendations not binding on the executive.
 
• Despite their limited powers, the councils provided a platform for **Indian leaders** to voice their concerns and grievances.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Act was introduced during the tenure of **Lord Dufferin** as the Viceroy of India.
 
• It was a response to the growing demand for **greater representation** and accountability in governance, as voiced by early Indian nationalists.
